attribution.note: Marcus wrote the characterisation himself, prompted by Altman's tweet. In the next paragraph he says he thinks this less rosy picture is closer to the mark.

semantics.note: This is a present-tense statement about ChatGPT as it was then. The claim correctly leaves out the rhetorical 'forced to acknowledge' framing.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: the version of ChatGPT then in use lacked broadly dependable general competence. 'Anything like' is treated as emphasis. The period is tied to Dec 2022 to Jan 2023.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own launch statement on unreliability. It is a company disclosure and predates the target period, so it is context only.
An independent evaluation of the 15 Dec 2022 version found about 63% average reasoning accuracy, called it an unreliable reasoner, and found hallucinations. Published before the evaluation date.
The same paper shows strengths on some tasks. That limits a literal reading but does not show broadly dependable human-level competence.

reviews.rationale: An independent evaluation of the December 2022 ChatGPT version found unreliable reasoning, about 63% average accuracy, and hallucinations. That meets the support condition. The strengths on some tasks do not amount to broadly dependable general intelligence, so the contradiction condition is not met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post. He attributes the $3M/day figure to rumours rather than asserting it.

semantics.note: The source sentence is garbled after 'millions'. The drafter rightly dropped that unclear clause. 'Super expensive' and 'modest' are firm. The rumour and 'perhaps' qualifiers on the figures are kept.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: high running cost, and 2022 revenue in the low tens of millions. Treating the $3M/day figure as a reported rumour rather than an assertion matches the words.

evidence.note: Press report, citing The Information, that OpenAI's 2022 revenue was about $28M. That is low tens of millions and modest.
Altman called the compute costs 'eye-watering' in Dec 2022. This is a statement by the company's own CEO, not an independent finding.
A contemporary independent estimate of $100K/day meets the contract's cost threshold. It also shows the rumoured $3M/day figure was overstated about 30-fold.
A later estimate (Apr 2023) of about $700K/day. It confirms costs were high but falls after the target period.

reviews.rationale: Reported 2022 revenue of about $28M fits 'modest, low tens of millions'. A contemporary estimate of $100K/day and the CEO's 'eye-watering' remark support high running costs. The rumoured $3M/day figure looks overstated, but Marcus credited it to rumour and did not assert it.

semantics.note: The claim captures the comparison but drops the 'I personally think' framing. It is a personal comparative judgment with no measure of closeness to AGI.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no comparison rule or proximity measure. Any test would need criteria the speaker did not supply.

reviews.rationale: This is a personal comparison between two overall pictures of OpenAI. It gives no measure of distance to AGI and no rule for deciding which picture is 'closer to the mark'. The narrower point about present capability is scored under claim 0c09b1.

contract.note: Reading 'rocketship' and 'typically' in the ordinary way is fair. The Q3 2022 comparison period was picked by the evaluator but is reasonable.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no representative financing records or survey showing how common an ongoing 75% profit allocation was among comparable startups. Semafor's report covers only this deal, so the typicality claim cannot be settled.
